quote: I had here you were the homeowner. Was it you and your wife?
stewart_read: Rep correctly identifies the wife as a co-owner on the title early, which is the right verify step, but never follows through to confirm she'll be present for the in-person quote.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as a protocol violation under spouse_decision, but that trigger requires spouse-deferral language ('I need to talk to my spouse') which never occurs here — the wife is simply a co-owner who needs to be on the appointment per verify.title_co_owners, a softer miss than an objection mishandled.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close the loop: once a co-owner is identified, explicitly confirm their attendance at booking rather than assuming it from context.

quote: I'll send you that paper as soon as I get to it, and I'll, put you down for tennis, Friday.
stewart_read: The appointment is explicitly contingent on the wife locating and sending the bill; the rep accepts this without pinning a backup plan if the bill doesn't arrive before Friday.
coaching_implication: Manager should flag that this booking carries real fragility — rep should have set a checkpoint (e.g., 'if we don't have it by Thursday, we'll still show up with an estimate range') to protect the sit.

quote: Somebody just kinda walking around and
stewart_read: Customer is asking what the actual appointment looks like — a chance to build anticipation about seeing his specific numbers — and the rep answers with logistics (duration) rather than tying it back to what he'll actually learn about his own home/bill.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to use appointment-length questions as an opening to create curiosity about the specific outcome (his design, his numbers) rather than just answering the clock question.

quote: Tomorrow is no good. Friday is. I have actually somebody else coming to give us a quote on a, new garage door.
stewart_read: Customer casually reveals he's actively collecting competing quotes for another home project the same week, a signal of a comparison-shopping mindset, but the rep doesn't probe or note it.
alternative_hypothesis: This isn't solar-competitive intel directly, so a strategic read is that the rep correctly didn't derail scheduling to chase an unrelated vendor mention.
coaching_implication: Minor miss — not urgent, but worth noting that the household is actively evaluating multiple vendors this week, useful context for the closer on how comparison-minded this customer is.

quote: My wife handles all that shit, man. I I I got a couple of businesses. I keep my head up.
stewart_read: Two active businesses plus a newly-opened retail shop suggest a household with above-average and possibly growing electric usage, but the rep doesn't tie this back to bill size or usage load.
coaching_implication: Rep could have asked a light follow-up connecting the business activity to home usage patterns as a way to build curiosity about his numbers, without pitching features or fabricating savings — e.g., simply noting that active households like his are exactly why the specialist looks closely at usage on the design call.

quote: And do you I know you you might not know, but do you have any idea of, like, an average price you guys are normally paying every month? No idea, bro.
stewart_read: Rep asks the bill question directly per script, but the customer has no number to give, and the rep accepts this without any fallback (e.g., asking for a ballpark range or checking if the wife might know).
alternative_hypothesis: Given the customer's genuine and repeated 'my wife handles that' framing, pressing harder in the moment risked frustrating him — deferring to the bill-photo collection later is a reasonable adaptation, not a pure miss.
coaching_implication: When the bill number isn't available live, the rep should still plant the emotional hook — e.g., framing the photo collection step as 'this is what lets us show you exactly what you're overpaying' — rather than moving past it as a pure data gap.

quote: Perfect. Well, we'll plan on that. I appreciate it.
stewart_read: The call ends without the rep restating the confirmed appointment details, without the one-hour block framing, without the no-driving/computer instruction, and without the 'is that fair?' handshake — button-up is essentially skipped.
coaching_implication: This is a clean, coachable gap: rep should always close with a full recap (day, time, format, duration, what customer needs to do) even on a friendly, easy call — the warmth of the conversation doesn't substitute for the mechanics.
